Applicant- Kripal Singh alias Sonu alias Kaka, who is in judicial custody in connection with FIR No. 99 of 2023, under Sections 376, 452 IPC and 3/4 of the POCSO Act, 2012, and bail rejection under Sections 452, 376 A, B of IPC and Sections under 5(m)/6 POCSO Act, registered at Police Station Kelakhera, District Udham Singh Nagar, has sought his release on bail.

entities.text: Kripal Singh alias Sonu alias Kaka
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text:
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
5.

Learned Senior Counsel for the applicant submits that there is delay in lodging the first information report as the incident took place on 31.07.2023 whereas the FIR was lodged on 01.08.2023; in the Medico Legal Report, the hymen of the victim is found intact and no internal or external injuries were found on the body of the victim.

Besides this, in the statement of Doctor, who conducted the medical examination, it has come that neither there was any injury in the internal part of the victim nor any sign of sexual assault was found on the body of the victim.
It has further been submitted that the applicant is languishing in jail 2025:UHC:3758 since 02.08.2023; that FSL Report does not connect the applicant with the alleged crime.
He submits that the applicant is about 27 years of age and in case, he is detained in jail for long, his entire career will be ruined.
He further submits that in case the applicant is granted bail, he will not misuse the bail and will furnish the bail surety as per the satisfaction of this Court.

6. Per contra, learned State Counsel though vehemently opposed the bail, but fairly conceded that,
perusal of the DNA report, reveals that neither traces of blood stains were found nor the semen was found on the trouser (salwar) and other clothes of the victim, which were sent for DNA examination.

BA1/584/2024 on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8939496/
1 7.
Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that the Doctor in her statement has submitted that the victim neither changed her clothes after the alleged incident nor she had taken bath.

8. Considering the submission of learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion as to the final merits of the case, this Court is of the view that the applicant deserves bail at this stage.
9. Accordingly the bail application is allowed.
10. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his executing personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of like amount, to the satisfaction of Court concerned.

(Alok Mahra, J.) 09.05.2025 Kaushal BA1/584/2024 on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8939496/
